input: Pack a go-bag for each family member this week

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Go-bags vary enormously — a 72-hour disaster kit, a travel bag, a car emergency kit, or a school bag. The type determines every item on the list.
The number, ages, and specific needs of family members (e.g., infants, elderly, pets) directly shape what goes into each bag and how many bags are needed.
The scenario the bag is designed for — natural disaster, power outage, evacuation, road trip — determines the contents and urgency.
A budget cap affects whether items need to be bought, sourced from home, or prioritised — and whether premium gear is on the table.
Whether bags are packed from scratch or topping up existing ones changes the immediate first action and effort level required.
Some families want lightweight and minimal; others want comprehensive and heavy. Prioritising weight vs. completeness shapes every packing decision.
Knowing what 'done well' looks like — a checklist signed off, bags stored somewhere specific, or reviewed by a certain standard — determines when the task is truly complete.

gold.taskTitle: Pack a go-bag for every family member
gold.taskDescription: Prepare a ready-to-grab emergency or travel bag for each person in the family, to be completed within the week.

questions.title: What type of emergency is this bag designed for?
questions.description: Identify the primary scenario — natural disaster evacuation, extended power outage, house fire, road trip, or general all-hazards preparedness — as this defines the entire contents list.

questions.title: How many people are being packed for, and what are their ages?
questions.description: Confirm the total number of family members and any special considerations such as infants, elderly relatives, people with medical needs, or pets, since each requires a tailored bag.

questions.title: Should the bags cover 72 hours, one week, or longer?
questions.description: Establish the intended duration of self-sufficiency the bag must support, as this scales the amount of food, water, medication, and clothing packed.

questions.title: What is your total budget for purchasing supplies?
questions.description: Determine how much money is available to spend across all bags this week, which drives decisions about buying new gear versus repurposing items already at home.

questions.title: Are you starting from scratch or updating existing bags?
questions.description: Find out whether bags and some supplies already exist and need refreshing, or whether everything needs to be sourced and assembled from zero, to set the right starting point.

questions.title: Should each bag be as light as possible, or fully comprehensive?
questions.description: Clarify whether the priority is grab-and-run portability with minimal weight, or thorough coverage of every scenario even if the bags are heavier and bulkier.

questions.title: How will you know each bag is truly finished and ready?
questions.description: Define the completion standard — for example, checked against a specific list, approved by all adults, stored in a designated spot, or reviewed by a professional — so the task has a clear finish line.
